Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, Cartify's usage has steadily exceeded the current hosted commit tier and we outlined a path that reduces per-token cost while guaranteeing headroom for seasonal traffic in Q3/Q4.

Quick recap and ask:
- Proposed uplift: move from Hosted Tier S (400M tokens/mo) to Hosted Tier L (1.2B tokens/mo) for the 12-month renewal window.
- Expected benefit: ~22% per-token cost reduction on average with an additional 15% burst credit allocation for peak days.
- Rate bands: baseline RPS will increase from 25 -> 75 rps for the committed pool; soft-throttle policy will apply after burst credits are consumed.

Can you confirm if the procurement timeline is still end-of-month? If yes, I'll prepare an official term summary and call out the DocuSign next steps. I'm CC'ing Karthik and Evelyn to confirm ops and CS details.

I've attached a short term summary and the SLA appendix for review.

Attachments: Cartify_Renewal_Term_Summary.xlsx (spreadsheet), SLA_Appendix.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Priyom

Elena / Samir —

Great questions, answered inline below. I've also attached a simple pricing CSV that shows year-one economics at the three candidate uplift levels.

1) Burst credits: these are allocated monthly and do not roll over. We provision 15% of the committed tokens as burst credits each month; unused burst credits are not carried forward but we do provide a monthly usage report and a one-time grace credit if there's a provisioning error.

2) Soft throttle fallback: we do NOT reject requests by default. When the committed pool + burst credits are exhausted, requests fall back to our lighter compute model (Model-Compact-v2) at a reduced RPS. This preserves successful responses with slightly higher latency and reduced contextual window (32K -> 16K tokens) rather than outright failures. If you'd prefer automatic region fallback, we can enable that as an opt-in policy.

3) Dedicated capacity: the uplift to Host Tier L remains a hosted (multi-tenant) offering. Dedicated GPU pools are available as an add-on if you want guaranteed instance-level isolation; we can price that separately.

Proposal summary (high level):
- New committed tokens: 1.2B / month (12-month term)
- Effective blended price: $0.0009 / token (vs current $0.00115)
- Monthly baseline RPS: 75 rps (burst up to 200 rps with credits)
- SLA: 99.95% regional availability (see attached SLA_Appendix.pdf)

Next steps:
- If this aligns, I'll open a HubSpot deal and send a DocuSign (Samir) with the above terms + standard Redwood T&Cs; legal edits are expected.
- CS kickoff (Evelyn / Marissa) — would be helpful to schedule a tech onboarding session during the first week of the contract.

Attachments: Commit_Pricing_Sheet.csv (csv)

Thanks,
Priyom

Priyom / Marissa —

Confirmed from an ops perspective: Hosted Tier L configuration supports the proposed baseline RPS of 75 and the described burst-credit gating. Notes:
- Autoscale warms in ~45s for sustained spikes; short, sharp spikes rely on burst credits.
- Soft-throttle fallback to Model-Compact-v2 will preserve request success but payload size may be truncated if context window exceeds 16K. We can instrument an early-warning webhook for Cartify to proactively purge large batched requests.
- No dedicated capacity is required to enable the uplift; if Cartify later requests dedicated GPUs we can provision a reserve with a 2–4 week lead time.

Marissa: please draft a 30/60-day onboarding checklist (technical onboarding + runbook for throttling behavior).

—Karthik
